intent: To demonstrate that high-income earners face a higher effective tax rate than the ultra-wealthy, and that the ultra-wealthy's tax burden has decreased since 2001.

units.meaning: In 2008, the $100k-$200k income group's effective tax rate (25%) was higher than the 400 richest' rate (18.1%), a gap of 6.9 percentage points.

basis.note: effective tax rate for the middle income group
effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accepted_routes: 25% vs 18.1%; $100k-$200k earners paid a higher effective rate than the 400 richest in 2008
The 400 richest paid 18.1%, lower than the 25% paid by $100k-$200k earners
Middle/high-income earners faced a 6.9 percentage-point higher effective tax rate than the ultra-wealthy in 2008
units.visual_evidence_rule: Two 2008 values must be visible/labeled: $100k-$200k (or middle) at 25% and 400 richest at 18.1%, on a comparable scale or with explicit comparison labels.
units.temporal_anchor: The first clause giving 25% and the clause saying the 400 richest paid just 18.1% in 2008.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly compare the 25% high-income rate against the 18.1% ultra-wealthy rate in 2008?

units.meaning: The 400 richest' effective tax rate declined from 23% in 2001 to 18.1% in 2008, a drop of 4.9 percentage points (about 21.3% lower relative to 2001).

basis.note: 2001 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns
2008 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accepted_routes: The 400 richest' effective tax rate fell from 23% in 2001 to 18.1% in 2008
The ultra-wealthy's rate declined by 4.9 percentage points since 2001
The top 400 rate was about 21% lower in 2008 than in 2001
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both top-400 values must be visible on a timeline or paired bars: 23% for 2001 and 18.1% for 2008, with a downward direction or change label.
units.temporal_anchor: The 2001 clause saying the rate was 23% and the 2008 clause saying it was 18.1%.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the 2001-to-2008 decline in the 400 richest' effective tax rate?

units.meaning: The $100k-$200k earners' effective tax rate in 2008 was 25%.

basis.note: effective tax rate for the $100k-$200k income group

accepted_routes: $100k-$200k earners faced a 25% effective tax rate in 2008
The $100k-$200k or middle-income group is shown at 25%
units.visual_evidence_rule: A bar/label for $100k-$200k or middle/high-income earners at 25% must be visible.
units.temporal_anchor: The first narration clause: 'If you earn between $100,000 and $200,000... up to 25% effective tax rate.'
units.reviewer_question: Is the 25% high-income effective tax rate required as a standalone visible value?

units.meaning: The 400 richest' effective tax rate in 2008 was 18.1%.

basis.note: 2008 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accepted_routes: Just 18.1% for the 400 richest tax returns in 2008
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2008 top-400 value must be labeled at 18.1% if shown as a standalone endpoint.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause: 'The 400 richest tax returns surveyed by the IRS paid just 18.1% in 2008.'
units.reviewer_question: Is a standalone 18.1% endpoint needed, or is it sufficiently covered by the 2008 comparison and 2001-to-2008 change units?

units.meaning: The 400 richest' effective tax rate in 2001 was 23%.

basis.note: 2001 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accepted_routes: In 2001, the 400 richest' effective tax rate was 23%
The 2001 baseline for the ultra-wealthy was 23%
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2001 top-400 value must be labeled at 23% if shown as a standalone endpoint.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 2001 baseline needed as a separate visible endpoint, or is it covered by the decline unit?

optional_valid: Highlight the 6.9 percentage-point gap between 25% and 18.1% as a derived comparison.
Show the 23% to 18.1% drop as an approximately 21.3% relative decline.
Frame the 400 richest' 18.1% as the lowest rate among the displayed groups in 2008.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that George W. Bush or any tax policy caused the decline.
Any 99% vs 1% wealth-share or tax-share figure, which is not in the table.
Payroll tax amounts or effects, which are not in the table.
Values for years or income groups other than 2001/2008 and the listed $100k-$200k and 400 richest groups.
Treating the 25% value as an exact rate for every $100k-$200k taxpayer if 'up to' qualifier is intended.
notes: All cited numbers are table values or arithmetic combinations of them. The core required story is the 2008 comparison (25% > 18.1%) and the 400 richest' decline from 23% in 2001 to 18.1% in 2008.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
